label: Power for a proposition: at w, y could initiate a causal chain issuing in p (a primitive)
term: power for a proposition (the PowerFor parameter)
definition: PowerFor w y p, for a world w, a being y and a world-proposition p: at w, y has a power whose exercise would initiate a causal chain issuing in p obtaining. A primitive Lean parameter of type W → B → (W → Prop) → Prop of TruthCore.Modal.ModalGrounding, constrained only by the premises that use it: Aristotelian grounding of a non-actual possibility (AristotelianGroundingFor, GlobalAbsenceGrounded), initiator presence (InitiatorPresentFor, GlobalAbsenceInitiatorPresent), concreteness of holders, and the OPEN transfer bridge to POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 (GlobalAbsencePowerIsPowerOverEsse, controls only).
note: Stipulated for #1887's reconstruction of Pruss's Aristotelian modality (analyst formulation; A. Pruss, 'The Actual and the Possible' and Actuality, Possibility, and Worlds, 2011, navigation only for this slice). Examples: a match's power to bring it about that a fire burns; a sculptor's power to bring it about that a statue exists. Non-examples: the bare logical possibility of p; a power whose exercise could not issue in p (a match and the proposition that two plus two is five). Distinct from POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 (DEF 3fd6bddb-f10c-4df4-8694-3eb5e7c28617): that relates a holder to one individual's being, this to a proposition, possibly a global one; the two are linked only by the transfer bridge. Distinct from CAUSE_2 (no exercise is implied) and from the C2 batch's PowerOver parameter. Structural properties assumed: none (not closed under entailment, not tensed). Pruss's account counts a power to initiate a chain that could lead to p; iterated powers (a power to produce something with a power) are not separately represented. Load-bearing use: in the #1887 routes PowerFor's target is a tenseless, negative state, global (no contingent concretum ever exists) or indexed to the actual world (none of the actual contingents ever exists). A chain that issues in a never-existing being is not a positive production, so the only available example is an abstention: a free agent able to refrain from producing or conserving anything (on classical theism, the creator's freedom not to create). No positive causal example is available, and this is principled: 'non-existence has no direct cause; for nothing is a cause except inasmuch as it has existence' (ST I q.104 a.3 ad 1, read by the parallel assessment slice; navigation only here), so a power for absence is either a potency in the thing or the withholding of a cause of its being. Trade-off: Pruss's own direction avoids this, since his holder is in the non-actual world and has a positive power for the actual world's being actual; but it needs the grounding principle applied at a non-actual world and S5 for that world to reach the actual one. Amendment (#1887 power-premise slice, docs/notes/pruss-power-premises.md): two readings of PowerFor must be distinguished. On the thin reading (a chain initiated by the holder whose outcome world satisfies p), positive production is also an example: a holder that produces a replacement array in a world lacking the actual contingents has a power for their joint absence (model replacementG), though it causes their absence neither directly nor indirectly. On the causal reading (the holder's exercise brings it about that p), ad 1 ('indirectly God can be the cause of things being reduced to non-existence, by withdrawing His action therefrom') and ad 3 ('a mere cessation of His action') allow an absence to be caused only by withdrawing a giving, so only withholding counts. The statement above that the only available example is an abstention holds on the causal reading only; the Lean parameter fixes neither reading. Open obligations: whether the chain's initiator exists in the world of the chain (initiator presence, tenseless); whether powers attach only to concrete beings; whether a power to abstain counts as a power in Aristotelian modality's sense.
